chunks: From him, from Al-Washa, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him) was asked, 'What equates to freeing a neck?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Feeding a Muslim man.'
ai.seo_question: What is the equivalent reward for freeing a slave in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elevates the act of feeding a single Muslim to the status of freeing a slave, emphasizing the profound spiritual weight of sustaining the believer. This equivalence underscores the Shia scholarly view that practical charity (sadaqah) serves as a direct means of spiritual liberation, mirroring the physical emancipation of a slave. It highlights the communal responsibility to nourish the faithful as a core component of faith-based social welfare.
